What changed (before → after):
Email check: read contractions, add offers, treat hint phrases as hints, and never drop an unreadable reply silently.
Before: (1) Rejection rules that rely on 'n't' miss contractions such as 'won't be moving forward', because the rule needs 'n't' at the start of a word. (2) 'High volume / large number of applicants' alone classifies a Rejection (Medium); 'high volume' itself has no rule. (3) There is no Offer type. (4) An email classified 'Other' is discarded without being counted or listed (JobSearch_Automation.gs, the email loop), so the application looks like no reply and auto-ghosts on day 45.
After: (1) Contractions read the same as 'not'. (2) Hint phrases ('high volume', 'large number of applicants') never decide alone: with a confirming phrase they take that phrase's type (Rejection, Offer, Next steps; 'we've received your application' confirms Received); without one, 'Couldn't tell'. (3) New Offer type, never auto-approved. (4) New 'Couldn't tell' handling: an unclassifiable email from a company I have an application with is listed in the summary with a link, and that row does not auto-ghost while it is unresolved.
Timing: a fix during the data cut (11/9-11/13/2026) under the break exception I approved 11/10/2026; recorded as a mid-cut change because it can move the email numbers.
Why (trigger and evidence): Two rejections were missed and proven 11/10/2026 on the real email text: Company A (10/22, Greenhouse) and Company B (10/26) both say 'won't be moving forward'; each classifies as Other, and changing only 'won't' to 'will not' makes each a High-confidence Rejection. Company A was auto-ghosted; Company B (tracker row 121) is still Waiting and set to auto-ghost 12/4/2026. The matcher was not the cause: Company A would have matched row 91 (High), Company B row 121 (Medium). False positive found the same day: the Company C 'team away' notice (10/19) was read as a Rejection (Medium) from 'received a large number of applications'; I caught it with a Manual Override. Fictional tests also showed offers and phrasings such as 'will not be progressed' and 'we'd like to have you meet the team' classify as Other. Risk: offers and interview invites can be dropped silently today (asymmetric cost: these are the emails I most need).
Acceptance criteria:
BEFORE DEPLOY (tests run by me before clasp push):
1. Regression: the real Company A (10/22) and Company B (10/26) emails classify as Rejection and match tracker rows 91 and 121.
2. Contractions: for every rejection rule that uses 'not', the 'n't' forms (won't, don't, can't, isn't, wasn't, weren't, haven't, aren't) classify the same as the 'not' form.
3. Hint rule: a hint phrase alone is never a Rejection. With a confirming phrase it takes that phrase's type; a hint plus a confirmation phrase ('we've received your application') is Received; with no confirming phrase it is 'Couldn't tell'.
4. Offers: offer emails classify as Offer, are never auto-approved, and always come to me.
5. No silent drops: an email the rules cannot classify, from a company I have an application with, is listed in the summary with a link; while it is unresolved, that row does not auto-ghost.
6. No harm: all existing test files pass; these real confirmations are never read as Rejection, Next steps or Offer, and never land in 'Couldn't tell': Company A (9/8), Company D (10/30), Company E (9/30), Company C 'team away' (10/19).
7. Coverage: the regression set includes at least one real email from each of Greenhouse, Ashby and Lever.
